acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Skeletons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Bone Champion, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Spur-Crown Formation Architect (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Bones fused into a solid armor-like mass while preserving joint gaps, with a horned skull and long bone spurs rising from the shoulders like a crown and matching seams at the hips.

Signature mechanic: Crownwork: the Champion plants one shoulder spur, draws loose bones into a curving wall, and completes it with the opposite spur to form a crown point. Bonesoldiers lock shields into the wall, Bone Knights levy through its interior channel, and Rattlers reform behind it. The Champion must keep one horned side turned toward each completed point, exposing the unfused hip seam on the opposite side.
battlefieldDuty: Fuse scattered remains into crown-shaped barricades that extend shield lines, define levy channels, and command lower skeletons through a deliberately breakable arena formation.
constructionDimensions: The remains become grave-mineral architecture through fossil-dense bone, sediment-packed joints, slate funerary plates, crystal runes at fusion seams, and carved tombstone shields or seal plinths.

Stance and reassembly become load-bearing: feet key into grave-soil sockets, ribs interlock like masonry, localized dust traces force through fused plates, and pale fractures open where mineral bone must articulate.
counterplay: Cross the planned curve before it closes, break the outermost shoulder-spur seam, or attack the hip opposite the Champion's turned horn; one broken crown point opens every lower-form route attached to it. Affinity signal: A crystal fusion seam turns chalk-white after a committed block, reassembly, or wall growth; breaking that seam scatters the supported bones beyond the binding path.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only earth treatment without fossil density, grave architecture, and changed load paths
Glow-only earth treatment without mineral fusion or readable fracture seams
Pasted rocks that conceal skeletal joints and negative space
Solid stone replacement that makes the form read as a generic statue or golem
identityInvariants: Human or humanoid skeletal proportions remain narrow, angular, and defined by empty negative space where flesh and organs would be.
Bone white or yellowed ivory is paired with rust, black iron, tattered grave-cloth, and one explained necromantic socket-fire accent such as green, blue, or gold.
Bone, rusted mail, corroded steel, grave-cloth, funerary jewelry, and crowns remain recognizable mortuary materials rather than living anatomy.
Carved skull runes, bone spurs, fused armor-like mass, grave regalia, and orbiting fragments accumulate as binding power becomes denser.
Bone density and the intensity and reach of the visible necromantic binding escalate together, but every form preserves gaps, joints, or binding anchors that can be deliberately broken.
telegraph: Shoulder spurs rise like crown tines, one horn on the skull aligns with a bone pile, and a bright binding line traces the planned curve across the floor before fragments move.
